title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (cote 140-3, 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'): Grothendieck studies group schemes over Z attached to the modular presentation SL2(Z) = <ρ,σ | ρ^3 = σ^2, σ^4 = 1>, with ρ of order 6 and σ of order 4.

Notation (inferred from this page and its neighbours):
- T_ρ and T_σ are the commutant tori of ρ and σ, i.e. the Weil restrictions R_{Z[ζ3]/Z}G_m and R_{Z[i]/Z}G_m. Their integer points are μ6 ≅ Z/6 and μ4 ≅ Z/4.
- N'_σ is a normalizer-type extension of T_σ by μ2, with μ2 acting on T_σ by σ ↦ εσ.
- T_0 is a further torus factor (probably the 'u' / determinant or base factor).
- SG is presumably SL2 or a similar reductive group, acted on by the group G*_{ρ,σ}(0) ⊂ T_0×T_ρ×N'_σ.
- 𝒯_{ρ,σ} is a subgroup cut out by determinant conditions; M_{ρ,σ} is the semidirect-type group built from these, and M°_{ρ,σ} its neutral or connected version.

The previous page proved that μ2 acts faithfully on 𝒯'_{ρ,σ}, the kernel of ε. Hence the centre of 𝒯_{ρ,σ} lies in that kernel and coincides there with the intersection with T_0×T_ρ×G_m.

This page summarizes this as (49):
- Centre(G*_{ρ,σ}(0)) = T_0×T_ρ×G_m.
- Centre(𝒯̂_{ρ,σ}) = (T_0×T_ρ×G_m) ∩ 𝒯_{ρ,σ}.
- SG*_{ρ,σ}(0) = {(u,a,λ) : u = λ^2, det a = ε'·(power of λ), ε'^2 = 1}, sitting in T_0×T_ρ×G_m.

By (47), the part of the centre acting trivially on SG is cut out by the extra condition u = 1. Then λ = ±1 and (det a)^2 = 1, giving (50): 1×ST'_ρ×μ2 ⊂ 𝒯̂ ⊂ T_0×T_ρ×N'_σ, where ST'_ρ = {a : (det a)^2 = 1}.

A tentative formula (51), Centre(M_{ρ,σ}) ≅ (1×ST'_ρ×μ2)×μ2 with the last μ2 ⊂ SG, is struck through. The margin reads (as I read it) 'Faux! le centre est plus grand'.

In the modular case he computes the group of integral points of the group (50) as (52): Z/6×Z/2×Z/2 ≅ Z/3×(Z/2)^3. This is a cyclic group of order 3, generated modulo something by -ρ, times (Z/2)^3, which he identifies with the group Σ of his section (IX). A marginal NB says this group is in fact contained in M°_{ρ,σ}(Z).

The page closes by announcing that the centre of M°_{ρ,σ} would be more interesting. The next page computes it: Centre(M°) ≅ (1×ST_ρ×ST_σ)×μ2, with integer points Z/6×Z/4×Z/2, and neutral component ST_ρ×ST_σ. Those formulas are again marked 'faux! centre de dim 3'.

The purpose is to understand the centres of the algebraic 'hulls' of the modular group used in his scheme-theoretic study of the loop equation, plausibly modelling π1 of M_{1,1} and the Teichmüller tower.
errors: Formula (51) for Centre(M_{ρ,σ}) is crossed out and declared false in the margin: the centre is larger. The computation via 'elements of the torus centre acting trivially on SG' misses central elements; the next page's margins likewise say 'faux! centre de dim 3'.
The group-theoretic identity Z/6×Z/2×Z/2 ≅ Z/3×(Z/2)^3 is correct.
The exponent in 'det a = ε'λ^?' is illegible. Consistency with u = λ^2 suggests a power of λ, possibly λ^2 or λ^3.

ideas.what: Computing centres of group schemes over Z built from the commutant tori of the order-6 and order-4 generators of SL2(Z) (Weil-restriction tori of Z[ζ3] and Z[i]) and their normalizers
ideas.modern_name: centres of reductive group schemes / maximal-torus normalizers over Z; algebraic envelopes of the modular group
ideas.where_published: SGA3 gives the general framework; this specific construction is unpublished

ideas.what: Identification of the integral points of the centre with Z/3×(Z/2)^3, a group Σ from his earlier section (IX)
ideas.modern_name: torsion of tori of integral points / centre of an arithmetic group

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine centre computations for tori and normalizers within an exploratory, partly self-corrected (marked 'faux') calculation. Nothing here stands as a new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: The vertical left-margin note is better read as 'Faux! le centre est plus grand,' rather than 'Jamais le centre plus grand'. It refers to the struck-out formula (51).
The second line of (49) has a struck-out word before (T_0×T_ρ×G_m).
In (52) the struck-out words are 'Groupe de' and the marginal NB reads 'NB Ce groupe est en fait contenu dans M°_{ρ,σ}(Z)'.
'det a = ε'λ^*' should be read as det a = ε'·λ^(exponent illegible), with 'det a' written above a struck-out symbol.
